patients.summary: Retired math teacher with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and glaucoma who joins in 2020, develops diabetic kidney disease stage 3b, has a resected pancreatic head adenocarcinoma, bullous pemphigoid, sigmoid diverticulitis, an inferior STEMI with contrast nephropathy, and after his last visit an admission for hypertensive pulmonary edema.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

Thomas is a 67 year old retired math teacher (taught high school for 34 years) establishing care after his internist retired. Prior records requested, not yet here.

HPI: Type 2 diabetes for roughly a decade, always on metformin, never on insulin. Does not check sugars often, maybe once a week fasting, 120s-130s. Blood pressure treated for over ten years, on lisinopril and a low-dose water pill, no lightheadedness. On atorvastatin for cholesterol without muscle aches. Has glaucoma, sees an outside eye doctor every 6 months or so, uses latanoprost nightly. Feels well. Walks most days, gardens.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, hyperlipidemia, open-angle glaucoma.
PSH: tonsillectomy as a boy (age 10). Screening colonoscopy at 63, told it was normal.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, HCTZ 12.5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, latanoprost 1 gtt OU qhs.
Allergies: none known to medications.
Family: father had a heart attack at 67. Mother had type 2 diabetes and glaucoma. Sister with high blood pressure.
Social: retired. Never smoked. A glass or two of wine a week. No other substances.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, claudication, polyuria, vision change beyond his usual, numbness in feet, GI or urinary complaints.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted. Fundi not visualized well through undilated pupils. Neck supple, no bruits. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Extremities without edema. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+, monofilament sensation intact both feet.

A/P:
1. Type 2 diabetes, on metformin. A1c, CMP today. Foot exam normal.
2. Hypertension, at goal on current regimen.
3. Hyperlipidemia, lipid panel today, continue atorvastatin.
4. Glaucoma, per ophthalmology. Asked him to have the eye doctor copy us on visit letters.
5. Health maintenance: will reconcile vaccines and screening once old records arrive. Flu shot at a nurse visit next month when the high-dose supply is in.

PHQ-2 negative. Follow up in about 4 months.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Fax, 38 pages, from his former internist's office. Contents: problem list (diabetes type 2, hypertension, high cholesterol, glaucoma), medication list matching what the patient reported, office notes 2017 to 2020, lab flowsheet, immunization record.

Pertinent: colonoscopy May 2016 to the cecum, no polyps, repeat in 10 years. Tdap 3/2017. PCV13 2/2018, PPSV23 2/2019. Childhood tonsillectomy noted in surgical history.

Abstracted to chart. Original to scanned media.

Your old records arrived yesterday and you are up to date on tetanus and both pneumonia shots. See you for the flu shot in October.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. Glad the numbers behave. I will book the flu shot with the front desk.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
INITIAL ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT

Health risk assessment reviewed with him. Independent in all ADLs and IADLs, still drives (says nights are getting harder, which he puts down to the glaucoma; due back at the eye doctor in June). No falls. Hearing fine. Lives in a single-level home. Exercise: walking 30 to 40 minutes most days. Diet: mostly home cooked, watches sweets.

Cognition: 3-word recall 3/3, clock draw normal.
Mood: PHQ-2 0.
Advance directive: has a health care proxy on file with his attorney, will bring a copy.

Screening: colonoscopy 2016 normal, next 2026. Hep C antibody today (never done). AAA screening not indicated, never smoked.
Immunizations: Tdap 2017, PCV13 and PPSV23 complete, COVID x2 done, flu done. Shingrix not yet, recommended at the pharmacy (covered under his drug plan).

Exam: BP and weight as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear. Feet with good pulses, sensation intact.

Plan: CMP, lipids, hep C today. Personalized prevention plan given. Diabetes visit in about 4 months.

documents.title: Wellness visit labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tom, results from yesterday: hepatitis C screen negative, which means no need to repeat it. Cholesterol numbers good on atorvastatin, kidney and liver tests normal. Remember the shingles shots at the pharmacy when you can.

documents.title: 90-day refills
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mail-order pharmacy requested 90-day supplies of metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, HCTZ 12.5 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg. Last visit 4/13, labs current. Approved x3 refills each per protocol. Latanoprost is prescribed by his eye doctor, not refilled here.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Visit Letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Re: Thomas Casey, DOB 01/09/1953
Date of visit: 06/25/2021

Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Casey for his scheduled glaucoma visit. He tells me night driving has become a struggle and that now and then he clips a doorframe or a chair he did not see off to the side. No pain, no redness in either eye.

Current drops: latanoprost one drop each eye at bedtime. Other medications include metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide and atorvastatin. No drug allergies. His mother also had glaucoma.

Examination:
Best corrected acuity 20/25 OD and 20/25 OS.
Applanation pressures 22 mmHg OD, 24 mmHg OS.
Anterior segments quiet, angles open.
Dilated fundus exam: cup-to-disc ratio 0.7 in each eye. No diabetic retinopathy, maculae flat.
Automated 24-2 fields: peripheral loss in both eyes.

Impression: primary open-angle glaucoma, both eyes, with peripheral field loss that fits his symptoms.

Plan: continue latanoprost nightly. We went over drop technique and the importance of not missing doses. Repeat visual fields in four months.

Thank you for allowing me to share in his care.

Ophthalmology

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine diabetes check. Feels well. Saw the eye doctor in June, letter in chart: pressures a bit high, fields worse, staying on latanoprost. Taking all his pills.
New: he noticed a brownish spot on his upper back some months ago and thinks it has gotten bigger. Not painful, never bled.

O: Vitals as charted. Upper back right of midline: round tan lesion about 1.5 cm, sharply bordered, slightly rough. Few scattered small brown macules elsewhere on the back. Heart and lungs normal. Feet normal.

Labs today: creatinine 1.2, potassium normal. A1c 7.0.

A/P:
1. T2DM, A1c 7.0, continue metformin.
2. HTN, at goal.
3. Lesion of back, growing per patient. Probably benign but I would like dermatology to see it and do a full skin check. Referral placed.
4. Flu shot in the fall; mentioned the covid booster when eligible.

RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
DERMATOLOGY CONSULTATION
Patient: Thomas Casey  DOB 01/09/1953
Visit date: 09/13/2021
Referred by: primary care, for an enlarging back lesion

History: 68 year old man who first saw the spot on his upper back several months back; since then it has grown slowly. It has not hurt, itched or bled. No weight loss, fevers or sweats at night. History of diabetes, hypertension, glaucoma. Medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, latanoprost drops. NKDA.

Exam: full skin examination performed. Upper back: a single round tan papule, 1.5 cm across, sharply demarcated, with a slightly rough, stuck-on surface. Nothing else on the skin looks like it. Scattered over the trunk and arms are multiple small, uniformly pigmented melanocytic nevi without atypical features.

Assessment:
1. Upper back lesion, benign on examination. No biopsy needed.
2. Multiple benign melanocytic nevi.

Plan: reassured. Return if the back lesion or any mole changes in size, color or shape, or bleeds. Sun protection reviewed.

Dermatology

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: diabetes recheck. Says he is up to the bathroom more and more thirsty than usual, going on a few months.

HPI: Otherwise feels fine. Taking metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ, atorvastatin every day without misses, pill box. Has been very strict with his eating since the holidays, cut out bread and desserts. No dysuria, hesitancy or weak stream. No swelling, no shortness of breath, no NSAID use.

Labs 2/8: fasting glucose 146, A1c 7.2. Creatinine 1.8, a clear step up from 1.2 in August. Urine albumin/creatinine 300 mg/g, first time we have measured it.

Exam: BP 132/86. Well appearing. Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft, no edema. Feet: pulses intact, sensation intact. Unremarkable overall.

A/P:
1. Chronic kidney disease, stage 3b by today's numbers (eGFR about 40), with heavy albuminuria. In a man with diabetes for over a decade and no other explanation this is diabetic nephropathy. Explained what the numbers mean. Repeat BMP and urine ACR in 3 months to confirm it holds.
2. T2DM, A1c 7.2. The thirst and frequency are more than I would expect for this A1c. Continue metformin. Keep up the diet.
3. HTN, BP 132/86, continue lisinopril and HCTZ.
4. Avoid ibuprofen and naproxen, Tylenol is fine.

RTC 3 months with labs.

documents.title: Question about kidneys
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Doctor, I have been reading about kidney disease stages since our visit. Being a math person I made a little chart of my creatinine. Should I be cutting back on protein? Is the wine ok? Thanks, Tom

documents.title: RE: Question about kidneys
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tom, good questions and I like the chart. No need to cut protein drastically; normal portions of meat, fish, eggs or beans are fine. A glass or two of wine a week is fine. The most useful things are what you are already doing: steady sugars, steady blood pressure, staying away from anti-inflammatory pain relievers. We will recheck in May.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: CKD and Diabetes
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back for the kidney recheck. Thirst has settled; he thinks he was simply drinking more because he was worried about it. No complaints today.

Labs today: creatinine 1.7s, holding in the same range as February. Urine ACR 280. Potassium and bicarbonate normal. Hgb normal. A1c 7.1.

Exam: vitals as charted. No edema. Heart and lungs normal.

Assessment: CKD stage 3b from diabetic nephropathy, now confirmed over 3 months. Stable.

Plan: same medicines. Labs every 6 months. Renally dose anything new. Next visit late summer.

documents.title: Kidney recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Tom, as we discussed yesterday, the creatinine is holding steady in the same range as February and the urine protein is about the same, so this is your new baseline. A1c 7.1. We will keep checking every 6 months.

documents.title: RE: Kidney recheck
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Understood. Added the new points to my graph. Tom

documents.title: Ophthalmology Annual Letter

Re: Thomas Casey, DOB 01/09/1953, seen 07/06/2022.

Annual diabetic and glaucoma examination. Continues latanoprost both eyes at bedtime with good adherence. Dilated exam: no diabetic retinopathy in either eye; optic nerves unchanged from last year. Fields stable compared with the fall study.

Plan: continue latanoprost, return in 6 months for pressure check and in 1 year for dilated exam.

orders.reason: postprandial vomiting, early satiety, weight loss

documents.title: Office Visit: Nausea and Weight Loss
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: stomach trouble, losing weight.

HPI: Since about mid-July he has felt full after a few bites and is nauseated most afternoons. In the last month he has vomited after larger meals several times, food that looks like what he ate. No blood, no black stools, no pain to speak of, just fullness up high. Weight down 7 lb from spring. Fasting sugars have crept into the 170s-190s though he has not changed his diet or pills, which surprised him. No fever, no jaundice, no change in stool color.

Meds unchanged: metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ, atorvastatin, latanoprost. No NSAIDs.

Exam: thinner. Vitals as charted, afebrile. Abdomen: mild tenderness in the epigastrium, fullness there that I cannot clearly define. No hepatomegaly, no jaundice. Rest normal.

A/P: Early satiety with postprandial vomiting of undigested food, weight loss and newly worse glycemic control in a 69 year old. Concerned about an obstructing process in the upper GI tract, including a pancreatic or gastric malignancy. Labs today (CMP, CBC, A1c, lipase). Urgent GI referral placed, front desk to call for the earliest slot. Small frequent meals, liquids if solids will not stay down, call if he cannot keep fluids down.

No change to metformin for now. Will call with labs.

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Tom. A1c 8.1, up from 7.1 in May. Hemoglobin 12.4, a little low and new for him. Liver tests and lipase normal, creatinine at his usual level. GI appointment confirmed for 10/17. Told him to call if vomiting gets worse in the meantime.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu L deltoid, Pfizer bivalent booster R deltoid. Tolerated. Weight checked at PCP request, down another pound. He is eating small meals, vomited twice this week. GI appt 10/17. Reinforced to call if not keeping fluids down.

events.reason: nausea, vomiting, early satiety, weight loss

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CONSULTATION
Patient: Thomas Casey  DOB 01/09/1953  Seen: 10/17/2022
Reason: urgent referral from primary care for vomiting and weight loss

HPI: 69 year old man with type 2 diabetes, stage 3 CKD and glaucoma. For three months he has had nausea that has steadily worsened, fills up quickly, and now vomits after meals; what comes up is recognizable, undigested food. He has lost 10 pounds over that time. His sugars have been running well above his usual for the past few weeks with no change in what he eats or takes. Metformin is his only diabetes medicine.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, latanoprost drops. NKDA.
Family history: father MI at 67, mother diabetes and glaucoma, sister hypertension.
Social: retired teacher, never smoker, occasional wine.

Exam: thin, not toxic. Mild epigastric tenderness. A firm mass can be felt in the upper abdomen. No jaundice, no lymphadenopathy, no ascites.

Data: Hemoglobin 12.1, WBC 7.0, platelets 250. Fasting glucose 180. CA 19-9 120 U/mL (reference 0-37).
Upper GI series (done the same day): contrast leaves the stomach slowly, with a narrowed segment at the distal stomach.

Impression: gastric outlet narrowing with a palpable upper abdominal mass, weight loss, new hyperglycemia and a raised CA 19-9. Pancreatic malignancy is the leading concern.

Plan: pancreas-protocol CT with IV hydration before and after given his kidney function, then endoscopic ultrasound with fine-needle aspiration. Discussed with him at length. Will update primary care as results come in.

Gastroenterology

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST, PANCREAS PROTOCOL (arterial and portal venous phases). IV hydration given per renal protocol.
Clinical: gastric outlet symptoms, palpable mass, CA 19-9 elevated.
Findings: 3.4 cm hypoattenuating mass in the pancreatic head. It compresses the second portion of the duodenum, narrowing the gastric outlet. No contact with the superior mesenteric artery, celiac axis or common hepatic artery. The mass abuts the superior mesenteric vein over less than 180 degrees without contour deformity. Common bile duct normal caliber. Liver without focal lesion. No ascites. No enlarged abdominal or pelvic lymph nodes. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Colon, bladder and bones unremarkable. Lung bases clear.
reports.conclusion: 3.4 cm pancreatic head mass compressing the duodenum, consistent with pancreatic carcinoma. Resectable by vascular criteria. No metastatic disease seen.

documents.title: CT Abdomen/Pelvis, Pancreas Protocol
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Report received electronically and filed. Pancreatic head mass 3.4 cm, resectable by vessel criteria, no metastases. Endoscopic ultrasound is scheduled by GI for 11/3.

reports.text:
Specimen: pancreatic head mass, EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration and cell block.
Microscopic: clusters of atypical glandular cells with nuclear enlargement, irregular nuclear contours and loss of polarity, in a desmoplastic background. Cell block shows infiltrating malignant glands.

documents.title: EUS-FNA Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
PROCEDURE: Upper endoscopic ultrasound with fine-needle aspiration, 11/03/2022. Monitored anesthesia care.
Findings: narrowed but traversable duodenal bulb and second portion. Hypoechoic irregular mass in the pancreatic head measuring about 34 mm, consistent with the CT. No liver lesions in the views obtained, no ascites. No suspicious nodes. Three passes with a 22-gauge needle, adequate per on-site review.
Complications: none.
Pathology (final 11/7): adenocarcinoma.
Plan: referred to surgical oncology for resection. Patient informed by phone today.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: Call after biopsy result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Tom after GI's report came through. He already heard from them yesterday; quiet on the phone but clear-headed. Surgical oncology consult this Friday. Offered to see him before or after, he would like to come in Thursday with his questions written down. Booked.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Visit: New Diagnosis Discussion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
40 minute visit, mostly counseling.

Tom brought a typed page of questions. We went through the CT and the biopsy: adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas, 3.4 cm, no spread seen, and the vessels look clear enough that a surgeon should be able to remove it. He sees surgical oncology tomorrow. We talked about what the operation involves, the recovery, that chemotherapy usually follows, and that the obstruction should resolve once the tumor is out.

Still vomiting a few times a week; tolerating soft foods and shakes. Weight 81 kg, down from 86 two years ago.

Diabetes: sugars higher, A1c 8.1 in September. Expect this may change after surgery. No change today.
Kidneys: told surgery and oncology about his CKD; renally dosed drugs.

He asked about a health care proxy; he has one, gave us a copy today for scanning.

Will touch base after his surgical visit.

medications.drug_text: lipase 24000 UNT / protease 76000 UNT / amylase 120000 UNT Delayed Release Oral Capsule
medications.sig: Take 2 capsules by mouth with each meal and 1 capsule with snacks

reports.text:
Specimen: pancreaticoduodenectomy.
Tumor: moderately differentiated ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head, 3.3 cm in greatest dimension, confined to the pancreas.
Margins: pancreatic neck, bile duct, uncinate/SMA, SMV groove, proximal and distal enteric margins all negative.
Lymph nodes: 0 of 21 involved.
Stage: pT2 N0.
reports.conclusion: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, 3.3 cm, margins negative, 0/21 nodes, pT2 N0.

documents.title: Surgical Oncology Discharge Summary
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 12/06/2022, discharged 12/14/2022
Procedure: open pancreaticoduodenectomy, 12/06/2022

Indication: 3.4 cm pancreatic head adenocarcinoma (EUS-FNA) with duodenal compression, resectable on imaging.

Course: operation without complication. Nasogastric tube out day 2, diet advanced from day 4, tolerating a regular diabetic diet by discharge. Drain output low and amylase normal, drain removed day 6. Blood sugars monitored closely in hospital; metformin resumed once eating. Creatinine stayed at his baseline. Wound clean.

Pathology: 3.3 cm moderately differentiated ductal adenocarcinoma, all margins negative, 0 of 21 nodes, pT2 N0.

Discharge medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; latanoprost both eyes at bedtime; NEW pancrelipase (lipase 24,000 units) 2 capsules with meals, 1 with snacks.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: surgical clinic 2 weeks; medical oncology referral placed for adjuvant chemotherapy; primary care within 1 week.

Surgical Oncology

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Transitional care visit, one week after discharge from surgical oncology (pancreaticoduodenectomy 12/6). Summary reviewed.

He is tired but eating better than he has in months, no vomiting since surgery. Takes the enzyme capsules with every meal; stools formed. Incision sore, no drainage. No fevers. Sugars 140s-180s fasting on metformin.

Meds reconciled: metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ, atorvastatin, latanoprost, plus pancrelipase. Nothing stopped.

Exam: afebrile. Midline/subcostal incision healing well, staples out at surgical clinic last Friday. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender. No edema.

Labs: creatinine at baseline, potassium normal. Hemoglobin 11.4, expected after surgery.

A/P:
1. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma, resected, pT2 N0, clear margins. Oncology consult 1/17 for adjuvant therapy.
2. Exocrine insufficiency after resection, on pancrelipase, working.
3. T2DM: allow a little latitude while recovering; recheck A1c in spring.
4. CKD 3b, stable through the hospital stay.
5. Postoperative anemia, recheck CBC with next labs.

medications.sig: IV on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle for 6 cycles, dose adjusted for renal function

documents.title: Medical Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION, 01/17/2023
Thomas Casey, 70 y/o

Diagnosis: pancreatic head ductal adenocarcinoma, pT2 N0, R0 resection 12/06/2022.

He has recovered well from surgery and is eating, on pancrelipase with meals. ECOG 1. Comorbidities include diabetes, CKD stage 3b (creatinine around 1.8), hypertension, glaucoma.

Postoperative CA 19-9: 28 U/mL (was 120 before surgery).

Discussion: adjuvant chemotherapy improves survival after resection. Given his age and kidney function, we chose single-agent gemcitabine rather than a multi-drug regimen. Plan gemcitabine on days 1, 8 and 15 of 28-day cycles for 6 cycles, starting 01/24/2023, with dose adjustment for renal function and CBC before each dose. Restaging CT chest and MRI abdomen at the end of treatment.

Medical Oncology

documents.title: Sugars on chemo days
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi Doc. Second cycle going OK, tired the day after but no vomiting. My fasting sugars are 160-190 the morning after infusion, then back to 140s. Do I need to change anything? Tom

documents.title: RE: Sugars on chemo days
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tom, a bump around infusion days is common during chemotherapy. Those numbers are acceptable for a few days at a time. Keep taking metformin and the enzymes. If you see readings over 300 or feel very thirsty or sick, call. We have an A1c planned for April.

events.reason: diabetes and CKD follow-up during chemotherapy

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes / CKD Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Cycle 4 of gemcitabine in progress. Fatigue the days after infusion, otherwise managing. Eating three meals with enzymes, weight steady at 77-78 kg. No vomiting. Sleeping fine. PHQ-9 4, says he is "more tired than sad".

A1c 7.6 (8.1 before surgery). Creatinine stable at his baseline, potassium fine. LDL at goal on atorvastatin. Oncology checks CBC with each treatment.

Exam: vitals as charted. Healed abdominal incision. No edema.

A/P: T2DM A1c 7.6, acceptable during chemotherapy, continue metformin. CKD 3b stable. HTN fine. Next visit after chemo finishes.

documents.title: Pancrelipase prior authorization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Drug plan requires prior auth for the pancrelipase capsules for the new plan year. Surgical oncology prescribed, but pharmacy faxed us. Completed with PCP: exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after pancreaticoduodenectomy 12/2022. Approved same day through 12/31.

documents.title: Final Infusion
documents.author: oncology
documents.body: Cycle 6 day 15 gemcitabine given, renally adjusted dose. Tolerated. Adjuvant course complete. Restaging and end-of-treatment visit scheduled.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Annual Letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Re: Thomas Casey, examined 07/07/2023.

Glaucoma and diabetic eye exam. Latanoprost continued nightly. Optic nerves stable in appearance. No diabetic retinopathy. Fields without definite progression.

Return 6 months.

Ophthalmology

documents.title: Medical Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY, 07/18/2023

Mr. Casey completed 6 cycles of adjuvant gemcitabine on 07/05/2023. Fatigue improving. No abdominal pain, eating well with pancrelipase.

Restaging: CT chest without contrast and MRI abdomen, 07/12/2023: postsurgical changes, no evidence of recurrent or metastatic disease.
CA 19-9: 19 U/mL.

Plan: surveillance with history, exam, CA 19-9 and imaging every 6 months.

Medical Oncology

documents.title: Finished chemo
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Oncology says the scans are clear and I am done with treatment. Thought you would want to know. Every six months for scans now.

documents.title: RE: Finished chemo
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is great news, Tom. Their letter came in this morning. Enjoy the summer, see you in September for your wellness visit.

medications.sig: Apply thin layer to affected skin twice daily; taper as directed

reports.text:
Specimen: punch biopsy, perilesional skin, left forearm, submitted in transport medium for direct immunofluorescence.
Direct immunofluorescence: linear deposition of IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone.
reports.conclusion: Linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone, consistent with bullous pemphigoid.

documents.title: Dermatology Visit
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
DERMATOLOGY
Patient: Thomas Casey  DOB 01/09/1953
Visit: 08/23/2023

HPI: Seen previously here in 2021 for a back lesion and moles. About two months ago he developed itchy, raised red patches across his trunk which he took for an allergy. In the last two weeks these have turned into large, taut blisters on the belly, arms and thighs. He has started nothing new, no new soaps or laundry products. History of pancreatic cancer resected last year with chemotherapy completed in July, diabetes, CKD, hypertension, glaucoma.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, latanoprost, pancrelipase. NKDA.

Exam: numerous tense bullae, 1 to 3 cm, sitting on erythematous skin of the abdomen, forearms and thighs; urticarial plaques ring several of them. Oral, nasal and genital mucosa clear.

Biopsy: punch from perilesional skin of the left forearm for direct immunofluorescence. Result 08/30: linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone.

Assessment: bullous pemphigoid.

Plan: clobetasol 0.05% ointment twice daily to the involved skin, including new spots; avoid systemic steroids given his diabetes. Taper over the coming months as it quiets. Follow up 6 weeks.

Dermatology

documents.title: Skin blisters
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI. I saw dermatology Wednesday for the blistering rash I mentioned to the nurse. They biopsied my arm and think it is something called pemphigoid. They gave me a strong steroid ointment. Itch is a little better already. Will let you know what the biopsy says. Tom

documents.title: RE: Skin blisters
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, Tom. That fits what you described. Use the ointment as they directed, keep the blisters clean and don't pop them. We have not received their note yet; I will ask for it. Let me know if any blisters look infected (spreading redness, pus, fever).

Interval: pancreatic adenocarcinoma resected 12/2022, adjuvant gemcitabine finished 7/2023, July restaging clear. Bullous pemphigoid diagnosed by dermatology 8/2023 (letter still not received despite a request; history from patient), on clobetasol ointment.

Functional: independent. Walking again 30 minutes daily. No falls. Still avoids night driving because of the glaucoma.
Mood: PHQ-2 1.
Cognition: no concerns from him, recall 3/3.

Skin: forearms and abdomen with fading pink patches and healed erosions, no tense blisters today. He is now applying once daily per derm.

Exam otherwise: heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft with healed incision, no edema. Feet: intact sensation and pulses.

Labs today: A1c 7.3. Creatinine at baseline. Hgb 12.6, recovering. Urine ACR 260. LDL at goal.

Prevention: high-dose flu and updated covid vaccines today. RSV vaccine recommended at the pharmacy (age, diabetes, CKD). Colonoscopy due 2026.

A/P: T2DM with CKD 3b, stable; HTN controlled; hyperlipidemia; pancreatic cancer in surveillance with oncology; BP improving on topical therapy; glaucoma per ophthalmology. Follow up in 4 to 5 months.

medications.drug: amoxicillin 875 MG / clavulanate 125 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 10 days

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST. IV fluids given before and after per renal protocol.
Clinical: LLQ pain, fever. History of pancreaticoduodenectomy.
Findings: Pericolic fat stranding around the sigmoid colon with a short segment of bowel wall thickening. No abscess. No free air. Postsurgical changes of pancreaticoduodenectomy without mass. Liver, spleen, adrenal glands and kidneys unremarkable. No hydronephrosis. Bladder normal. No enlarged nodes. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Acute uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis. No abscess or perforation.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Patient: Thomas Casey, 71 M. Arrived 06/20/2024 13:40.

CC: left lower belly pain x 3 days.

HPI: Dull, steady ache low on the left, getting worse over three days, with a low-grade fever, nausea and not much appetite. Looser stools the past two days. No vomiting, no bright red blood, no dark tarry stools. Has had a couple of milder bouts of this before that went away on their own; this one will not let up.
PMH: pancreatic adenocarcinoma resected 2022 with chemo afterward; CKD stage 3 from diabetic kidney disease; diabetes; hypertension; glaucoma; bullous pemphigoid. Colonoscopy in 2016, normal.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ, atorvastatin, pancrelipase, latanoprost. NKDA.
Social: never smoker, occasional wine.

Triage vitals: T 38.2 C (100.8 F), BP 128/74, HR 94.
Exam: uncomfortable but nontoxic. Abdomen tender in the LLQ, no rebound, no guarding. Bowel sounds a bit decreased. Rectal: normal tone, no mass, brown stool.

Labs: WBC elevated. Creatinine at his baseline. Urinalysis without signs of infection or blood.
CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast (renal hydration protocol): sigmoid fat stranding and wall thickening, no abscess, no free air.

Dx: acute sigmoid diverticulitis, uncomplicated.
Dispo: tolerating oral fluids, pain controlled with acetaminophen. Discharged home on amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily for 10 days, clear liquids advancing to low-residue diet. Return for worsening pain, high fever, vomiting or bleeding. Follow up with PCP within 1 week; consider colonoscopy after recovery.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
COLONOSCOPY, 08/29/2024
Indication: CT-proven sigmoid diverticulitis 06/2024; prior colonoscopy 2016.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: good (BBPS 8).
Findings: scope advanced to the cecum, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve photographed. Scattered diverticula in the sigmoid colon. Mucosa otherwise normal throughout. No mass, no stricture, no polyps.
Impression: sigmoid diverticulosis. No evidence of neoplasm.
Recommendation: high-fiber diet. No further screening colonoscopy needed at his age unless new symptoms.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: Cardiology Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 06/13/2025 via the emergency department; discharged 06/17/2025.
Principal diagnosis: inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
Secondary: contrast-induced nephropathy on CKD stage 3b.

Presentation: 72 year old man with diabetes and CKD who came in about two hours after the start of chest pain spreading into his left arm, with breathlessness and sweating. BP 160/90, HR 102, RR 22. Glucose high on arrival, consistent with his diabetes under stress. Baseline creatinine 1.8, eGFR 40. ECG: ST elevation in II, III and aVF. STEMI alert.

Course: emergent coronary angiography via right radial artery with limited contrast: occluded right coronary artery, treated with one drug-eluting stent with good result. Pain resolved in the lab. Echo 06/15: EF 50%, inferior hypokinesis. Creatinine rose to 2.6 on hospital day 2 after the contrast and was 2.2 at discharge, urine output preserved; metformin held 48 hours after contrast and then resumed. Uneventful telemetry.

Discharge medications:
- aspirin 81 mg daily (NEW)
- clopidogrel 75 mg daily (NEW), do not stop without talking to cardiology
- metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily (NEW)
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily
- lisinopril 20 mg daily
- hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily
- metformin 1000 mg twice daily
- pancrelipase with meals
- latanoprost both eyes at bedtime
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with a BMP; cardiology in 8 weeks; cardiac rehabilitation referral placed.

Cardiology

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit: Inferior MI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Transitional care visit. Discharge summary has not reached us; history from Tom and his hospital paperwork (medication list and the instruction sheet he brought).

Admitted 6/13 with an inferior STEMI, one stent to the right coronary artery. He was told the dye affected his kidneys and that he should have blood work. Home 6/17.

Since discharge: no chest pain, no dyspnea at rest, walking around the house and yard. A little lightheaded standing up fast the first two days, gone now. No bleeding or bruising. Taking all medicines; showed me the bottles.

Meds reconciled: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 25 (all new), atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, metformin 1000 BID, pancrelipase, latanoprost.

Exam: vitals as charted. Right wrist access site healed, radial pulse good. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

Labs: creatinine 2.0, down from what he was told in the hospital, still above his baseline of 1.8. Potassium normal. Hgb stable, platelets normal.

A/P:
1. Inferior STEMI, s/p drug-eluting stent to RCA. Dual antiplatelet therapy; reviewed that clopidogrel must not be stopped without cardiology. Cardiac rehab referral was placed by the hospital, he will call them. Cardiology in August.
2. Contrast-induced nephropathy on CKD 3b, improving. Recheck BMP in 6 to 8 weeks. Avoid NSAIDs, stay hydrated.
3. T2DM: metformin was held 48 h and resumed per his sheet.
4. HTN: BP fine on the regimen.
5. Records request for the discharge summary.

RTC 7 weeks.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 06/16/2026 through the ED; discharged 06/19/2026.
Diagnosis: acute pulmonary edema with severe hypertension.

Presentation: 73 year old man with type 2 diabetes, CKD stage 3, a history of contrast nephropathy, inferior MI with RCA stent (06/2025) and resected pancreatic cancer. While watching television in the evening he became suddenly, severely short of breath and began coughing up pink, frothy sputum. On arrival RR 30, BP 180/100, HR 110, SpO2 85% on room air. Crackles to the mid-lung fields on both sides, jugular venous pressure up, 2+ pitting edema of both legs. Creatinine 1.8, his baseline. BNP markedly elevated. Chest film: pulmonary edema with cephalization and septal lines. ECG: inferior ST elevation, unchanged from his 2025 tracing; no new ischemic change, catheterization not felt to be indicated.

Course: nitroglycerin infusion, IV furosemide and noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation in the ED, with rapid improvement; weaned to room air the next morning. Echocardiogram EF 50%, unchanged. Blood pressure controlled on his home regimen.

Discharge medications: furosemide 20 mg daily (NEW); aspirin 81 mg; clopidogrel 75 mg; metoprolol succinate 25 mg; atorvastatin 40 mg; lisinopril 20 mg; hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg; metformin 1000 mg twice daily; pancrelipase with meals; latanoprost both eyes at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: cardiology in 2 weeks; primary care.

Cardiology
